A new chapter for St Mary’s. Co-educational from 2027.
ABOUT US
At St Mary’s School in Gerrards Cross, we believe in a holistic approach to education, where every student is encouraged to embrace their unique potential.
Our nurturing environment fosters a sense of belonging, enabling each individual to feel valued and supported on their educational journey. We are dedicated to empowering our students with the knowledge, skills, and confidence they need to navigate an ever-changing world.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's School Our Ethos - St Mary's School
pageCache.text:
Learning for Success in Nursery School and Reception
At St Mary’s, academic rigor is a priority. As an independent school following National Curriculum guidelines, we have the additional freedom to build an exciting and innovative curriculum that fits the needs of our pupils based on their collective interests as well as their academic strengths and weaknesses. Our adjoined Nursery and Reception classrooms allow us the option of operating as an integrated unit where we can meet individual needs. For example Nursery pupils who are ready for more challenge can join Reception for maths and phonics and where some of our Reception pupils can join Year 1 for mental maths, reading and phonics.
From Nursery, the pupils take part in daily mathematics, English, phonics and reading sessions and enjoy specialist teaching in French, music, ballet, PE and Forest School throughout the week. Small class sizes, with two teachers and at least two full time members of support staff, mean that we know each student individually – their strengths, weaknesses and what type of learner, and can deliver teaching and experiences accordingly. This bespoke approach to learning ensures individual academic success from day one.
There is also a range of enrichment activities available to our Nursery and Reception pupils including lunchtime and after school clubs such as gymnastics, art and sports skills. Engagement in these builds important skills including teamwork, commitment, and problem solving which contribute to overall success. We also have a variety of interesting external visitors, and school trips throughout the year to enhance our pupils’ learning outside of the classroom.
Our aim is that when the pupils reach the end of Reception, they feel successful, resilient and confident, ready for the move up to Year 1.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's School Pastoral Care and Well-being in Prep School - St Mary's School
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care and Well-being
During a student’s time in our Prep School at St Mary’s, we endeavour to nurture their confidence and well-being and safeguard their mental health – this applies to every student from our youngest to our oldest. We are striving for every student to have positive mental health, and to know how to maintain this. They should feel safe and emotionally secure with resilience and self-belief. We encourage our pupils to recognise what they have achieved and learnt, whether it be social, emotional or academic. They can then take those achievements throughout their school career and beyond.
In the Prep School, our pupils enjoy a hands on and varied pastoral programme called ‘HeartSmart’. This progressive curriculum has five strands which cover all aspects of personal, social, health and economic education. As part of the programme, pupils have:
Our school counsellor is a proactive member of our Prep School community. Her open door approach gives girls another person to speak to if they need support or advice. Our counselling team also hosts regular assemblies with the girls about broader topics such as friendships and navigating their way through any issues that may arise.
The importance of communication can never be underestimated in well-being. We are proud to operate an open door policy throughout our Prep School to ensure we know what is going on at home, and can support students at school, and vice versa. Parents are encouraged to talk to staff at pick up or, if they require a longer meeting, to simply email to arrange an appointment. We truly believe that an open dialogue is the best approach to holistic and consistent care both inside and outside of school.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's School Wrap Around Care for Nursery & Prep School - St Mary's School
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
We understand the daily demands of busy working families and are here to make your life easier with our Wrap Around Care provision. After school care in the Prep School is directed, while in Senior House, pupils can independently complete homework or read.
Our Breakfast Club is free for pupils who are not eating breakfast.
For those who need breakfast, it is available at a minimal cost of £1 per item.
Nursery and Reception children can be dropped off from 7:30 AM and are supervised in Paddington House.
Years 1-6 can be dropped off at 7:30 AM and attend Breakfast Club in the Dining Hall, where they participate in various activities to start their day.
Senior House students arriving before school begins must sign in at Reception, then head to their Form Room, Library, or attend one of our co-curricular clubs.
The Hub, our after school care for Prep students, is free and available until 6:00 PM. Located in Paddington House, The Hub offers structured time for Prep pupils to stay at school until 6:00 PM, either after the school day or following co-curricular clubs.
You can book The Hub in advance using the booking form, but we also accept last-minute bookings through the school office.
An example of The Hub’s weekly timetable is available below.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's School Nursery & Reception - St Mary's School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Little St Mary’s Nursery and Reception
Welcome to Nursery and Reception – based in our dedicated Little St Mary’s building – where your child’s happiness and well-being is at the heart of all that we do! From day one, they will become part of our school community where academic rigor is a given, and where a wide range of opportunities are available to all.
You only have to look through the window, or step inside our purpose-built setting to experience the happiness, engagement and enthusiasm of our pupils. Our varied curriculum, in both Nursery and Reception, includes Forest School, French, swimming, music, art and ballet, allowing pupils to immerse themselves in an exciting variety of activities – enabling them to explore the world around them, whilst building the skills and confidence that will inspire and engage them to fulfil their potential. This, combined with maths, phonics, literacy and reading provides the perfect start to each student’s education journey.
Our open-door policy encourages parents to be involved in their child’s learning. Events including open classrooms, craft mornings, tea parties and parent breakfasts allow our pupils to share their excitement about their school and their learning with their parents (and even Grandparents!).
At St Mary’s, we accept pupils into our Nursery the term after their 3rd birthday, and our ethos is quite simply that happy children will succeed!
A Day in the Life of Nursery at St Mary’s
St Mary’s offers pupils an education up to the age of 18. The benefits to being part of a 3-18 school for those in our Nursery School and Reception are vast; from having older students to aspire to, friendships with girls from all year groups, access to facilities and specialist teachers and a comforting familiarity at every point in their journey through St Mary’s.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's School Forest School - St Mary's School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
For an afternoon a week, pupils in Little St Mary’s explore our dedicated Forest School site. It is certainly a highlight for many – not only is it an opportunity to let off steam but the bug hunts, talking trees, fire lighting, and activities using natural materials allow our pupils to immerse themselves in nature and explore the world in which we live.
Run by our qualified Forest School teachers, Forest School sessions encourage pupils to learn how to take risks safely, and to build key skills including resilience, self-esteem, and confidence through experimenting with and investigating the world around them. Forest School is based on learning through unplanned, child-initiated learning opportunities – imaginations are empowered to run wild and pupils are encouraged to direct their own learning based on their interests.
The value of outdoor play and learning, moving around, exploring the woodland around us and connecting to nature, is highly important as it supports the pupils’ mental health and well-being.

The School Day
The youngest students in our school, those who are new to childcare, or in their first year of Primary School, are adapting to new routines and a culture of learning during their time in Little St Mary’s. Through tailored teaching experiences and enriching activities, a love of learning is instilled and pupils feel happy and secure to take risks and challenge themselves to prepare them for the exciting primary school journey that lies ahead.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's School Careers and Higher Education - St Mary's School Careers
pageCache.text:
Careers and Higher Education
Girls at St Mary’s School, Gerrards Cross, benefit from bespoke one–to–one careers support from our dedicated Higher Education Coordinator as they navigate their journey towards higher education. Our commitment to helping each student achieve her individual academic and career aspirations is an essential part of our Sixth Form experience.
Our Approach
We understand that every student is unique, with individual interests, strengths, and goals. Our UCAS coordinator works closely with each student to provide personalised guidance tailored to her specific needs and aspirations. Each student will receive recommendations for suitable courses and universities based on individual preferences and academic achievements.
Whether students are considering traditional universities, art schools, degree apprenticeship schemes, or other specialised universities, we have the expertise to offer tailored advice. With guidance about applications, choices, and writing personal statements students are supported every step of the way.
Those considering applications to Oxbridge and those applying to competitive courses such Dentistry, Medicine and Veterinary Science follow a unique and speciailised pathway including interview coaching with subject specialists.
Personal Statement guidance at St Mary’s offers comprehensive support in crafting a compelling and unique personal statement including identifying what to include to ensure each application stands out against others. Through thorough review and feedback every statement showcases each individual’s strengths and aspirations.
Students receive tailored preparation for admissions tests (e.g., UK Clinical Aptitude Test, LNAT, BMAT, etc.). Throughout their time in Year 11 and into Sixth Form, students enjoy mock interview sessions and feedback to help them excel in interview scenarios.
Many of the applications from our students require slightly different paperwork or processes. Students receive continuous support throughout the application process including assistance with any additional paperwork or requirements.
All our Year 13 students gain admission to their dream universities and go on to pursue fulfilling next steps. Our school’s UCAS support has a proven track record of helping students achieve their goals. Most of our students move on to Russell Group universities, some opt to study as far afield as Canada and Korea, whilst others apply for apprenticeships, take a gap year or train in the arts at specialist colleges.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's School Results and Leavers' Destinations - St Mary's School
pageCache.text:
Results and Leavers’ Destinations
A level students at St Mary’s in Gerrards Cross have been celebrating their A level examination results today. This creative and inspiring group of students have been exemplary role models to their peers throughout Year 13 with their strong leadership qualities, enthusiasm and camaraderie; they have, today, continued to be an inspiration to younger students with their A level results and plans for their next steps.
They have achieved places at an exciting range of courses including Chemical Engineering at Nottingham, Chemistry at Warwick, Marine Biology at Plymouth, Economics at Birmingham, Journalism and also History at Cardiff to name but a few. All of our students are either going on to a chosen University or Further Education establishment and some will be taking gap years to complete courses and travel; all looking forward to very bright futures ahead. They leave St Mary’s equipped with the passion, skills and self-belief to be exactly who they want to be and to follow their dreams and we can’t wait to hear what they will be doing in years to come.
We are proud of all of our students’ achievements; in particular, the Art, Music, Drama, Dance, Music, Religious Studies and Sociology Departments achieved 100% A*-B grades. With an overall 64% A*-B grades and a 100% pass rate, the cohort has much to celebrate today.
We will be celebrating all the girls’ achievements reflected in these A level grades with their teachers and parents, as we wish them well for their future courses and careers. We look forward to keeping in touch with the families and welcoming the girls back to St Mary’s in the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's School St Mary's Commended in Prestigious Independent Schools of the Year Awards 2026 - St Mary's School
pageCache.text:
St Mary’s Commended in Prestigious Independent Schools of the Year Awards 2026
St Mary’s School is delighted to announce that it has been recognised in the prestigious Independent Schools of the Year Awards 2026, receiving Commended status in not one, but two national award categories: Sporting Achievement and Careers Provision.
The awards celebrate excellence and innovation across the independent education sector, recognising schools that provide exceptional opportunities and outcomes for their pupils. This year attracted a record number of entries from hundreds of schools across 25 categories, making the recognition even more significant.
The commendation reflects St Mary’s commitment to delivering an outstanding all-round education. From elite sporting pathways and leadership opportunities to an ambitious careers programme that prepares students for an ever-changing world of work, the school continues to ensure every girl is equipped to thrive both inside and beyond the classroom.
Commenting on the announcement, Mr Lars Fox, Head, said:
We are incredibly proud to have been recognised nationally for both our sporting achievement and careers provision. These commendations are a testament to the dedication of our staff, the enthusiasm of our students and our commitment to providing an education that develops confident, capable and future-ready young women. It is wonderful to see the breadth of opportunities we offer being recognised on a national stage.
Dr Helen Wright, Chair of the Independent Schools of the Year Awards 2026, praised this year’s entries, describing the innovative and life-affirming experiences offered by independent schools as “awe-inspiring”, with the standard of submissions “never higher.”
St Mary’s now looks ahead to the next stage of the awards, with finalists due to be announced in September ahead of the national awards ceremony in October.
This latest recognition follows another exceptional year for the school, reinforcing St Mary’s reputation for excellence in both academic and co-curricular education, where every girl is encouraged to discover her passions, develop her talents and realise her full potential.

Our scholars play an active role in school life, embracing leadership opportunities and acting as inspiring role models within the St Mary’s community.

Our Aims & Values
At St Mary’s, our aims and values are at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to providing an excellent, aspirational education within a caring and happy community, where every pupil is known as an individual, encouraged to believe in themselves and supported to achieve their full potential.
Our holistic approach combines academic ambition with outstanding pastoral care and a rich range of opportunities beyond the classroom. We want every pupil to leave St Mary’s with the knowledge, skills, confidence and character to embrace opportunities, overcome challenges and make a positive contribution to the world around them.
Our Aims
Our Values
Character education is a deliberate and purposeful part of a St Mary’s education. Alongside academic achievement, we develop the values, behaviours and personal qualities pupils need to thrive at school and throughout their lives.
By encouraging pupils to develop both academically and personally, we support their wellbeing while building the confidence, resilience and self-belief to pursue their ambitions. We want our pupils to be ready for an ever-changing world, equipped not only with knowledge but with the curiosity, adaptability and strength of character to respond positively to new opportunities and challenges.
Our TAKE CARE values bring this approach to life. They represent the character strengths we encourage every St Mary’s pupil to develop:
Together, our aims and values provide the foundations for a St Mary’s education: developing confident, compassionate and ambitious young people who are ready to embrace their future and make a positive difference in the world.

Our Community and History
Our sense of community and History is very important to us as a School and our unique environment allows us to foster an inclusive community spirit, not only amongst the girls but also with parents and in the wider community.
1872
St Mary’s School was established in 1872 in Paddington, then a relatively wealthy area of London, by the Anglican Foundation of The Sister of the Community of St. Mary the Virgin, Wantage. It was one of the earliest establishments to reflect changing Victorian attitudes to the education of women.
1901
In 1901 the Anglican Foundation of the Sisters relinquished control of the School. In the years which have followed, though the extent of the religious teaching in the school has changed, St Mary’s has remained committed to the beliefs and ethics of the Church of England, although girls of all religions and denominations are warmly welcomed.
1911
In 1911 came the school’s first move and for a while, an alteration of name. The school moved to Lancaster Gate where it was known as St Mary’s College, a change possibly brought about by the development of a teacher’s training College alongside the Junior and Senior Schools.
1937
1937 saw the second move with St Mary’s Junior and Senior Schools relocating to Gerrards Cross, initially based in a house in Orchehill Avenue, before moving to its present more spacious site in Packhorse Road. In 1937 this house was owned by the Sharpe family and the freehold was sold by Harrods for the princely sum of £7,000! Prior to this, in 1842, the estate was purchased by William Blount, who had recently married Lady Charlotte, daughter of the Duke of Somerset. The house was greatly enlarged and altered, with Gothic windows and tall chimneys. Inside, the drawing room was enhanced with a highly ornate raised ceiling (now the Senior School library).
1970
St Mary’s School grew and grew. For a short period in the 1970s boys were admitted up to the age of seven, but that practice stopped and St Mary’s has been an all-girls school since then. There was also a period when St Mary’s had a boarding house (now the Nursery and Key Stage 1 part of Prep).
2022
Like any organisation with over 150 years of history, St Mary’s has a strong sense of tradition. It is our firmly held belief that this accumulated experience provides a strong base upon which to build for the future. In 2016 our modern Sixth Form block was opened and 2018 heralded the latest addition to our excellent facilities with the opening of Cherry Tree House, a modern classroom block, housing six spacious classrooms, all equipped with the latest technology. In September 2020, our new Early Years building, Little St Mary’s, opened and Michaelmas Term 2021 saw the completion of our new Multi Use Games Area, complete with floodlights. At St Mary’s we never stand still and ongoing initiatives ensure that we continue to grow and thrive.
2023
The Summer of 2023 saw our driveway and turning-circle re-surfaced, new canopies in the Rose Garden for outdoor dining and a well-being pod for student use. We welcomed Alberto, or Bertie, as he is known to the school community as our new well-being dog.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's School GCSE Results - St Mary's School
pageCache.text:
Each year we are incredibly proud of the GCSE results achieved by our Year 11 students. Through dedicated teaching, an inspiring commitment to study from students, and a calm approach to exams, our pupil’s excel year on year.
GCSE Results 2025
The excellent GCSE results achieved by St Mary’s School’s Year 11 students reflect their hard work, determination and commitment throughout their GCSE courses. Building on the strong foundations developed in Years 7–10, students approached their examinations with maturity, focus and resilience, supported by excellent teaching, structured revision programmes and strong pastoral care.
This year, 45% of all GCSE grades were awarded at Grades 9–7, with 26% at Grades 9–8 and 9% achieving the highest possible Grade 9. Overall, 70% of all grades were awarded at Grades 9–6.
GCSE Results Highlights
While these headline figures demonstrate the strength of academic achievement at St Mary’s, they tell only part of the story. We are particularly proud of the individual progress behind every grade. Each student followed their own journey through GCSEs, overcoming different challenges, developing confidence and working towards their own ambitions.
Our results reflect the strong value-added education at St Mary’s. We recognise the potential of every individual and provide the teaching, challenge, encouragement and pastoral support needed to help each student achieve their aspirational best.
Year-on-Year Academic Success
Consistently strong academic outcomes across consecutive years.
We are proud to share our students’ remarkable performance over the past three academic years. Our results demonstrate long-term academic strength and real consistency in high-quality outcomes:
Nearly half of all grades awarded are at the highest levels. This reflects our students’ dedication and the quality of teaching and support they receive.
